repository.name: battery-thermal-modeling-notes
repository.title: Battery Thermal Reasoning Lab
repository.description: Trace battery heat-generation assumptions, compare cooling boundaries & reproduce a transparent one-node energy balance.
repository.summary: Research notes and templates accompany a dependency-free thermal model with selectable integration methods and heat terms. The browser isolates the simplest linear balance before returning to the richer native reference.
repository.audience: Battery and BTMS learners reviewing heat sources, boundaries, numerical methods, and validation evidence.

model.equation: ΔT = (Q/h) · (1 − exp(−h · 60t/C)); T = Tₐ + ΔT; heat removed = hΔT; stored heat = CΔT/1000.
assumptions: One uniform thermal mass starts at ambient temperature.
Constant heat input and linear heat transfer; no phase change or spatial gradients.
Elapsed time is shown in minutes; the energy-balance calculation uses seconds.
The browser starts at ambient and uses constant heat and convection; parameters are not fitted to a named cell.
The native model’s explicit Euler, exact-linear, and RK4 methods have different valid use cases; the browser uses only a closed form.
A calculated temperature or limit crossing does not establish thermal-runaway behavior or a safe operating limit.
model.introduction: This exact one-node linear response is a warmup for the native model’s scheduled boundaries, entropic heat, temperature feedback, radiation, and integration options. Those additional terms are not active in the browser.

modules.title: Declare the thermal control volume
modules.objective: Identify heat input, heat rejection, and stored energy before reading a temperature curve.
steps: Read the governing balance in models/README.md.
Apply 1,200 W heat, 40 W/K conductance, 18,000 J/K capacity, and 25°C ambient.
Predict the 30 K steady rise and inspect the temperature and heat stored after ten minutes.
modules.reflection: Which physical volume does the lumped temperature represent, and what measurement could test that interpretation?

modules.title: Change thermal inertia alone
modules.objective: Distinguish a slower transient from a lower steady temperature.
steps: Keep heat, conductance, and ambient fixed.
Double thermal capacity to 36,000 J/K and predict the ten-minute response.
Scrub toward sixty minutes and explain why the same steady-state rise is approached more slowly.

checkpoints.label: Residual net heating after ten minutes

modules.reflection: What mass and specific-heat evidence would you place in the parameter traceability matrix?

modules.title: Move the boundary without changing generation
modules.objective: Separate ambient temperature from heat input and heat-transfer conductance.
steps: Return capacity to 18,000 J/K and raise ambient from 25°C to 40°C.
Predict the change in absolute temperature and whether stored heat above ambient changes.
Read the variable-cooling profile to see how the native reference can schedule boundary changes by interval.

checkpoints.label: Heat above ambient retains the same ten-minute value

modules.reflection: Why should a radiative-surroundings temperature be recorded separately from convective ambient temperature?

modules.title: Choose a model and verification path
modules.objective: Decide which terms and numerical checks the next engineering question requires.
steps: Double conductance to 80 W/K at 25°C while retaining 1,200 W and 18,000 J/K.
Verify the 30-minute result and near-zero net heating.
Use the native model guide to decide between exact-linear integration and RK4 when adding nonlinear surface radiation.

checkpoints.label: Residual net heating is below 1 W

modules.reflection: Draft a verification plan covering equilibrium, signs, conservation, step-size convergence, and the measurements still needed for validation.
